description: Creates a new monitor from a name, a type and the fields that type requires. Choose the type with listMonitorTypes, preferring one made for the service over a generic port check, then call getMonitorTypeFields for its required and optional fields, their defaults and where each is passed. A create that lacks a required field is refused rather than saved as a monitor that fails every check. A push monitor's generated token and ping URL are returned. To change an existing monitor use updateMonitor.

active.description: Whether the monitor starts checking immediately (default: true). Pass false to create it paused.

databaseConnectionString.description: Connection string for the database monitor types. A credential.

databasePassword.description: Password for mysql monitors, if not in the connection string. A credential.

databaseQuery.description: Query a database monitor runs. Omit for the type's default.

description.description: Free-text description shown on the monitor page

dns_resolve_server.description: DNS server to use for resolution (required for dns type, default: 1.1.1.1)

dns_resolve_type.description: DNS record type to query (dns and globalping; default: A)

docker_container.description: Docker container name (required for docker type)

docker_host.description: Docker host ID (required for docker type). Use listDockerHosts to find available IDs.

domainExpiryNotification.description: Notify before the domain registration expires. Needs Uptime Kuma 2.1 or later.

expectedValue.description: Threshold the json-query result is compared against. Stored as a string.

expiryNotification.description: Notify before the TLS certificate expires (http, keyword, json-query, globalping)

hostname.description: Hostname or IP address to check (port, ping, dns and most non-HTTP types)

interval.description: Check interval in seconds (default: 60, or 300 for ntp; min: 1)

jsonPath.description: JSONata expression for json-query monitors. Must resolve to a primitive.

jsonPathOperator.description: Comparison operator for json-query monitors. UP while value <operator> expectedValue.

keyword.description: Keyword to search for (keyword monitor type)

maxretries.description: Max retries before marking as down (default: 0)

method.description: HTTP method (GET, POST, etc.) for http type

notificationIDList.description: Map of notification IDs to enable (e.g. {"1": true, "3": true})

port.description: Port number (port, and other types that take one)

pushToken.description: Push token for push monitors — the secret in the ping URL. Omit and one is generated and returned.

resendInterval.description: Resend notification every N checks while down (0 = disabled, the default)

retryInterval.description: Retry interval in seconds when monitor is down (default: the interval, min: 1)

tags.description: Tags to assign to the monitor

timeout.description: Request timeout in seconds. Omit for the type's default, which getMonitorTypeFields gives. Avoid 0: Uptime Kuma turns a stored 0 into a timeout of about 13 hours, so the monitor never reports DOWN.

type.description: Monitor type (e.g. http, port, ping, dns, push, keyword). Use listMonitorTypes for all options.

typeFields.description: Fields specific to the monitor type, e.g. {"mqttTopic": "sensors/#"} for mqtt or {"bearer_token": "…"} for an HTTP monitor behind authentication. Call getMonitorTypeFields with the type for the names, meanings and allowed values — they are validated, and an unknown name is refused. getMonitor returns these fields at the top level of the monitor; to change one, pass it here.

upsideDown.description: Invert status — treat up as down

url.description: URL to check (http, keyword, json-query and other URL-based types)

name: createMonitor

authMethod.description: Only when authMethod was inferred from the credentials passed. The method that was stored.

pushToken.description: Push monitors only. The token, so the sender can be wired up without a second, wider read.

pushURL.description: Push monitors only. The URL the sender should GET.

timeout.description: The timeout in seconds actually stored, including the default applied when omitted.
